analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy (03 November 2026)
key_insights: Midterms day. Polymarket gives Democrats a 95% chance of winning the House and 79% of retaking the Senate. The S&P 500 has been higher one year after all 20 midterm votes since WWII.

Democrats need a net gain of 3 House seats (current split 220-215) and 4 Senate seats (Republicans hold 53-47, and VP Vance holds the tiebreak). RealClearPolitics averages show Democrats ahead in North Carolina, Alaska, Texas, Maine, Ohio and Kansas, all Republican-held.

Even one Democratic chamber constrains Trump's legislative agenda, including spending packages and debt ceiling increases. A Democratic Senate would also limit presidential nominees, including Fed Governors. Trump keeps veto power, which needs two-thirds of both chambers to override.
Final results may not be known by morning. In 2024 the AP called the House for Republicans 8 days after the election. The new Congress convenes January 3.

Brent Jan 2027 contract fell -7.63% to $104.77/bbl on hopes for a US-Iran resolution. Triggers included an Axios report that Trump wanted to give diplomacy more time, Iran's Supreme Leader authorising peace talks, and positive comments from Trump and VP Vance. Oil is up half a percent this morning on a WSJ report of a US strike on Qeshm Island that has not been widely picked up.

The S&P 500 reversed an early +1.08% gain to close -0.51%. The Nasdaq 100 fell -1.39% into technical correction territory, -10.36% from its October 6 peak, led by the Philly semiconductor index at -3.37%. There was no overt catalyst. Expectations of a blue wave may be weighing on tech because a Democratic win could create hurdles for data center buildout and bring more AI regulation.
The equal-weighted S&P 500 rose +0.73% with more than two thirds of the index advancing, continuing the pattern of tech losses masking broader equity resilience.

Apple reported fiscal Q3 sales of $114.5bn vs $113.5bn expected and guided gross margin to 45-46% vs 47% estimated. Shares fell about 3% after hours, after a -1.83% regular session. Apple remains the world's most valuable company, narrowly ahead of Nvidia.

Rates and Europe: 10yr UST yield fell 1.6bps to 4.91%, the lowest since early September. Bunds fell 3.1bps, OATs 7.3bps and BTPs 8.9bps, tightening the Franco-German spread by 4.2bps. The STOXX 600 rose 0.42% to its highest since early September. The Treasury's refunding set Q4 borrowing at $618bn (revised -$10bn) and Q1 at $800bn, at the high end of expectations.
Overnight Asia: KOSPI -3.76% after US tech losses, S&P futures -0.19%, Nasdaq futures -0.12%, Stoxx futures -0.87%. The Nikkei was closed. The PBOC reiterated stock-market support measures.

The RBA raised its cash rate 25bps to 4.85%, a fifth hike this year and an 18-year high, in a split decision with three of nine members favouring a pause. It raised its trimmed mean inflation forecast to 3.6% for December (from 3.3%) and now sees inflation at the 2.5% target midpoint by June 2028, six months later than before.
South Korea October CPI rose 2.8% y/y vs 2.9% expected and 2.9% in September. Core was 2.8%, unchanged. The Bank of Korea meets Nov 26.

market_movers.rationale: Reported Q3 sales of $114.5bn vs $113.5bn expected but guided gross margin to 45-46% vs 47% estimated. Shares fell about 3% after hours.

sector_views.rationale: Chip sentiment deteriorated, with the Philly semiconductor index down 3.37% and the Nasdaq 100 in correction. The report notes a possible Democratic win could raise hurdles for data center buildout and AI regulation. This is a description of market moves, not a stated rating.

risk_factors: Escalation in the US-Iran conflict after the midterms, including the unconfirmed WSJ Qeshm Island report.
Continued AI and chipmaker sentiment deterioration, with the Nasdaq 100 in correction.
A Democratic win bringing hurdles for data center buildout and more AI regulation.
Elevated US fiscal needs, with Q1 borrowing estimated at $800bn.
A close House or Senate race could delay the result by days.
vol_and_positioning: Further Fed hikes/cuts priced for 2026 at 18bps, unchanged. Further ECB hikes/cuts priced for 2026 at 21bps, unchanged.
The equal-weighted S&P 500 rose +0.73% while the cap-weighted index fell, showing tech losses masking broader resilience.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: hopes of a diplomatic resolution after Iran's Supreme Leader gave the government powers to hold peace talks and Trump and VP Vance gave positive comments.
A WSJ report of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, not widely picked up, contradicts the recent dovish commentary.
There had been fears of an escalation shortly after the midterm elections.
US midterm elections on November 3 covering the full House, a third of the Senate and 36 governors.

tension_points.bull_case: The equal-weighted S&P 500 rose +0.73% with more than two thirds of the index advancing, and the STOXX 600 hit its highest since early September, showing broad resilience.
tension_points.bear_case: The Nasdaq 100 is in technical correction at -10.36% from its October 6 peak, with chip stocks down sharply and Apple guiding margins lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic win that creates hurdles for data center buildout and a push for more AI regulation would deepen the tech selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Peace talks authorised by Iran's Supreme Leader and positive comments from Trump and Vance sent Brent down 7.63% and yields lower.
tension_points.bear_case: A WSJ report of a US strike on Qeshm Island, not widely picked up, pushed oil up half a percent this morning and contradicts the dovish commentary.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Confirmation of the US strike on Qeshm Island, or renewed escalation after the midterms, would reverse the oil decline.
